profile.reading:
Tahoe Reno 1 sits at 1 Superloop Circle, McCarran, Nevada, the founding building of Switch's "Citadel Campus" in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, adjacent to the Tesla Gigafactory. Switch announced the campus in January 2015 as a 1,000-acre, roughly 1 billion dollar development targeting 3 million square feet at full build-out, then described it as 2,000 acres and up to 7.2 million square feet at up to 650 megawatts in a February 2017 press release marking the facility as "now open," giving Tahoe Reno 1 itself 1.3 to 1.36 million square feet and 130 megawatts (130 MVA) of power capacity, over 83,000 tons of cooling, a proprietary tri-redundant UPS power system, and Switch's patented "SHIELD" dual independent roof decks rated to withstand 200 mph winds behind a 20-foot solid concrete perimeter wall. Switch's FY2021 SEC 10-K filing, its last as a public company before the 2022 DigitalBridge/IFM take-private transaction, lists Tahoe Reno 1's year as 2016 at 99 percent utilization, a year that predates the February 2017 "now open" press event, likely reflecting phased occupancy ahead of a formal opening ceremony. Switch has since dramatically expanded its stated ambitions for the full Citadel Campus, with current marketing describing up to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion, several times the 2017-era figures, reflecting AI-era demand growth since the 2022 ownership change. Switch names NV Energy as an early solar-development utility partner and has since built the large "Gigawatt Nevada" solar-and-storage project, whose Storey County-serving portion alone totals 127 megawatts of solar and 240 megawatt-hours of battery storage, to help power the Citadel Campus with renewable energy.

Storey County's Tahoe Reno Industrial Center spans roughly 107,000 acres and hosts more than 100 tenants beyond Switch, including Tesla's Gigafactory and Google, drawing more than 900 megawatts of on-site power generation capacity across the broader industrial park from multiple power plants, per public county and industrial-park descriptions. Nevada's data center tax abatement program under NRS 360.754 offers a 10-year abatement for a minimum 25 million dollar investment and 10 Nevada jobs, or a 20-year abatement for a minimum 100 million dollar investment and 50 jobs, both requiring pay at or above the statewide average wage; while Switch's own materials describe the program's general terms, no source found this session names Switch specifically as a confirmed recipient at the Citadel Campus.

The same press release specifically names TAHOE RENO 1 as the campus first building, describing it as up to 1.3 million square feet and up to 130 MW of power capacity, a tier-1 operator figure for this specific building, given as an up to design target rather than a confirmed current operating figure, so also not applied to critical_it_mw.

reading.body:
Tahoe Reno 1 is the first building of Switch's Citadel Campus, a 1.3 million square foot facility in Storey County, Nevada, opening in 2016 with a published design capacity of up to 130 megawatts of power. At an assumed 350 kilowatts per rack, a typical density for GPU clusters, 130 megawatts of IT load would equal roughly 370 racks, though the operator publishes this figure as a design target rather than a confirmed current operating level. The building sits in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center adjacent to Tesla's Gigafactory, where 900 megawatts of on-site generation capacity serves more than 100 other tenants across 107,000 acres.

Nevada publishes capacity figures from only two data center operators statewide, totaling 10.37 megawatts across 26 mapped facilities, making Tahoe Reno 1 the third-largest published capacity in the state. The facility qualifies under NRS 360.754 for Nevada's data center tax abatement program, though the operator's participation at this campus is not confirmed in published sources. The broader Citadel Campus holds stated expansion targets of up to 650 megawatts across 7.2 million square feet, with current marketing describing ambitions up to 17.4 million square feet and 2 gigawatts at completion, reflecting growth since the 2022 ownership change.

The campus has contractual access to renewable power through the Gigawatt Nevada solar and storage project, which includes 127 megawatts of solar capacity and 240 megawatt-hours of battery storage serving Storey County. Switch completed Tahoe Reno 1 with proprietary infrastructure including tri-redundant UPS power, dual independent roof decks rated for 200 mph winds, and 83,000 tons of cooling capacity. The site's growth trajectory and scale in a jurisdiction with limited published capacity density make its expansion plans material to Nevada's ability to supply future AI workloads.
